newsitem.title: FRANCE: Le Monde criticises West over Lebanon silence.
newsitem.headline: Le Monde criticises West over Lebanon silence.

text.p: Lebanese exiles urged France on Friday to help release detainees in Beirut as the daily Le Monde criticised Paris for a low profile reaction to a wave of arrests of Lebanese Christians by Beirut's Syrian-backed government.

The Rally for Lebanon (RPL) said 15 people detained in the latest swoop were still being held and "reiterated its demand to French authorities to intervene so that all political detainees in Lebanon are released".

RPL, which is close to exiled Lebanese Christian former military leader General Michel Aoun, asked French President Jacques Chirac this week to intervene and requested an emergency meeting with Foreign Minister Herve de Charette.

Recalling that international human rights groups alleged the detainees were tortured, the influential Le Monde wrote: "Syria's behaviour is not surprising. But the incomprehensible silence of the West seems each day to legitimise the Syrian occupation (of Lebanon).
"France's president who claims to be a 'great friend' of Lebanon has become mute. And there is elegant cynicism at the foreign ministry which says it "wants to stay informed," Le Monde wrote.

"Does France's much heralded Arab policy mean that one can accept the violation of human rights in a country and among a community is close to France ? We hope to be proved wrong soon," the centre-left paper wrote.
The wave of arrests followed an incident last week in which attackers machinegunned a van carrying Syrian workers in a Christian area of Lebanon, killing the driver and injuring passengers.
The Lebanese army said it was part of a wave of attacks aimed at wrecking Lebanon's close ties with Syria and serving only the interests of Israel.
With 35,000 troops deployed across Lebanon, Damascus is Lebanon's main power broker and the two countries closely coordinate all peace moves with Israel.
Lebanese Prosecutor-General Adnan Addoum said on Monday that 26 of 48 detainees had been freed. He said none of the detainees had been charged with any offences.
Lebanese Christian opposition politicians at home and in Paris initially put the number of detainees at 200.
The RPL listed the names of the 15 people it said were still held. It said others were released in return for signing statements saying they were not mistreated.
Among those held are Wael Kheir, head of a Lebanese human rights group, and journalist Pierre Atallah of the conservative Beirut newspaper An-Nahar newspaper, it said.
